points.title: What SQL is
points.must: SQL = Structured Query Language, the standard language to create, manage and query relational databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL…); declarative — says what, not how.

points.title: DDL definition
points.must: DDL = Data Definition Language: defines / changes the structure (schema) — tables, fields, types, keys; commands CREATE, ALTER, DROP.

points.title: DML definition
points.must: DML = Data Manipulation Language: works with the data / records in the tables; commands SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE.

points.title: DDL vs DML comparison
points.must: A comparison (table) of DDL and DML: purpose, commands, what is affected (schema vs records), an example of each.

points.title: SQL data types
points.must: A data type is the kind of data a field stores; it decides the values accepted, the storage and the operations possible; INT, FLOAT/DOUBLE, DECIMAL(p,s), VARCHAR(n), CHAR(n), TEXT, DATE, DATETIME, BOOLEAN — each with an example field.

points.title: CHAR, VARCHAR, DECIMAL and choosing types
points.must: CHAR(n) is fixed length (padded), VARCHAR(n) up to n characters; DECIMAL(p,s) = p digits in total, s after the point; Phone numbers, IIN and codes as text (leading 0 / +); money as DECIMAL; dates as DATE; yes/no as BOOLEAN — with the reason.

points.title: Constraints
points.must: PRIMARY KEY, NOT NULL, UNIQUE, DEFAULT, CHECK, AUTO_INCREMENT, FOREIGN KEY … REFERENCES and what each does.

points.title: CREATE DATABASE / CREATE TABLE
points.must: A full CREATE TABLE example: one line per field with name, type (size) and constraints, commas between lines, primary key, closing );.

points.title: ALTER TABLE
points.must: ALTER TABLE … ADD field type; MODIFY; DROP COLUMN; RENAME COLUMN — with an example; records stay, structure changes.

points.title: DROP, and DELETE vs DROP
points.must: DROP TABLE / DROP DATABASE delete the structure and all the data; cannot be undone — back up first; DELETE = DML, removes records, structure stays; DROP TABLE = DDL, removes structure and data; DROP COLUMN removes a column.

points.title: INSERT syntax
points.must: INSERT INTO Table (fields) VALUES (values); values in the same order, text in quotes, AUTO_INCREMENT key left out; several rows at once.

points.title: Queries and SELECT basics
points.must: A query is a request to the database in SQL; a SELECT returns a result set (a table); SELECT * / chosen fields FROM table; DISTINCT removes duplicates — with examples.

points.title: SELECT columns, WHERE rows
points.must: SELECT chooses the columns, WHERE chooses the rows; the table itself is not changed (diagram or example result).

points.title: WHERE operators, AND vs OR
points.must: =, <>, <, >, <=, >=, AND, OR, NOT, BETWEEN (inclusive), IN, LIKE with % and _, IS NULL — each with an example; 'Books of A and B' means pub = A OR pub = B / IN (A, B); AND on one field returns no rows.

points.title: Worked example of SELECT
points.must: A task broken into columns → table → rows → the final query (e.g. vegetarian meals under 900 tenge).

points.title: UPDATE syntax
points.must: UPDATE Table SET field = value [, field2 = value2] WHERE condition; calculation from the old value (price = price * 1.1); An UPDATE with WHERE and the rows before / after, showing only matching rows change.

points.title: DELETE syntax
points.must: DELETE FROM Table WHERE condition; removes whole rows, no field list; without WHERE all records go but the table stays.

points.title: WHERE warning
points.must: UPDATE / DELETE without WHERE affect every record; use the primary key for one record; test with SELECT first.

points.title: SQL style rules
points.must: Keywords in capitals, text and dates in single quotes, numbers without quotes, statement ends with ;, no spaces in names.

points.title: Common mistakes
points.must: At least two: spaces in names, missing / extra commas, DELETE instead of DROP COLUMN, SELECT called DDL, VARCHAR without size; At least two: missing quotes, SET after WHERE, DELETE field FROM, = with a pattern instead of LIKE, AND instead of OR.
